title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (Premium): hold reports for GCC, GCC High and DoD
summary: Hold: the briefing presents seven days as a maximum age for hold-status data, but the cited warning does not guarantee that maximum. It also incorrectly calls the roadmap the only Microsoft source about the Government release, despite citing three Government deployment pages that describe it.

claims.claim: The preview page warns that hold-status data can be up to seven days old, implying a seven-day maximum age.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery hold report no more than once every seven days up to seven days. Read edisc-hold-report: the status warning says 'no more than once every seven days'; three-to-seven-day full-sync text concerns case-name and case-status updates, not a guaranteed maximum status age.
claims.fix: Replace 'The commercial preview page warns that the data can be up to seven days old' with 'The preview page warns that policy and location status sync no more than once every seven days and might not reflect recent hold changes'. Keep the advice to check the specific hold in its case.

claims.quote: The report syncs policy and location status no more than once every seven days, so the information shown might not reflect recent changes to your hold policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; controls[0].note; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The general eDiscovery permission controls are documented, but their Government report applicability is described as unconfirmed.
claims.quote: To use eDiscovery capabilities and features in the Microsoft Purview portal, assign the appropriate permissions to users.
claims.fix: Replace the Government access-model caveat with: 'Microsoft documents these permissions for eDiscovery capabilities and features in the Microsoft Purview portal; the Government deployment pages still list hold reports as In development.' In the impact rationale, attribute the named report-viewer roles to the documented preview rather than a separately confirmed Government access model.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The report page describes viewing and downloading information, not changing holds through the report.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery hold report read only report change holds. Read full edisc-hold-report and edisc-hold-report-script; report steps describe view, sort, filter, group, customise and download. Hold remediation is described separately, not as a report write operation.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Why it matters
claims.claim: Policy failed identifies incorrectly configured policies that are not enforced and directs administrators to create a rule and resync.
claims.quote: The policy doesn't have a rule or was set up with rule set as disabled. These policies aren't enforced even if the policy status is successful. To ensure these policies are enforced, create a rule and resync the policy.

claims.claim: A location held under several policies appears repeatedly and contributes repeatedly to the location-in-policy item count.
claims.quote: If the same location is placed on hold under different policies, the same location appears multiple times in the report under the respective case and hold policy and contributes to multiple item counts.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Role groups > eDiscovery Manager > Edit > Choose users reaches role assignment.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Role groups. ... select eDiscovery Manager. ... Select Edit. ... On Manage eDiscovery Manager, select Choose users or Choose groups.
claims.fix: Use 'Settings > Role groups > eDiscovery Manager > Edit > Manage eDiscovery Manager > Choose users'. In the note, state that this first selection assigns Managers; the documented wizard subsequently offers Choose users to assign Administrators.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group> assigns the eDiscovery Managers subgroup.
claims.quote: Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group>
claims.fix: Keep the documented command, but add to controls[0].note: 'The group supplied to -Member must be a mail-enabled security group; this command assigns the eDiscovery Managers subgroup, not the Administrators subgroup.'

claims.claim: A mail-enabled security group cannot be added to the eDiscovery Administrators subgroup.
claims.quote: However, you can't add a mail-enabled security group to the eDiscovery Administrators subgroup.
